whatItDoes: AI! and AI? trigger focused Pi follow-up turns from editor comments; AI. supplies context without triggering a turn.
Only actionable markers trigger a turn; context markers supply surrounding information.

whenToReachForIt.invocation: Start or inspect the watcher with /watcher, then write supported markers in a configured text file.

situations.when: A code review note should become a focused implementation turn
situations.use: Place an intent marker beside the relevant code.

situations.when: A question belongs next to the source that prompted it
situations.use: Place a question marker and let the watcher carry file context into Pi.

situations.when: Nearby comments should guide but not trigger work
situations.use: Use context markers alongside one actionable marker.

whatItAdds: Debounced file watching across configured roots without following symlinks.
Marker parsing, focused turn dispatch, and guarded cleanup after settlement.

howItFits.relationship: Watcher handles small editor-driven follow-ups; Ralph handles durable plan-driven iterations.
Explanatory guidance can add code-specific learning notes to watcher-triggered implementation turns.

questions.question: What can change in the source file?
answer: Live watching is an interactive editor workflow, only actionable markers trigger a turn, and handled comments may be removed after completion.

workingIf: Saving a supported actionable marker creates one focused follow-up turn.
After settlement, handled marker comments are removed only within the guarded source path.
setupNotes: Created and maintained by Vedang under the WTFPL.
The package needs interactive Pi, configured roots, and supported text files.
Behavior claims were reviewed against the installed Git revision.
